   140→/* Display Config WiFi info in visually pleasing format */
   141→void DevUtils::SerialBanners::printWiFiConfigBanner(const char* apPassword, WiFiManager& wifiManager) {
   142→    String network = wifiManager.getConfigPortalSSID();
   143→	String password = apPassword;
   144→	if (password.length() == 0) {
   145→		password = "No Password Set (Open Network)";
   146→	}
   147→	String ipAddr = WiFi.softAPIP().toString();
   148→
   149→	String networkInfo = "Network: " + network;
   150→	String passwordInfo = "Password: " + password;
   151→	String ipInfo = "IP Address: " + ipAddr;
   152→
   153→	int maxLen = max({ networkInfo.length(), passwordInfo.length(), ipInfo.length() });
   154→
   155→	String dashLine = DevUtils::repeatString("─", maxLen + 2);
   156→
   157→	String formatStr = "│ %-" + String(maxLen) + "s │\n";
   158→	String headerStr =
   159→		"┌" + dashLine + "┐\n"
   160→		"│ Connection to WiFi Portal%*s│\n"
   161→		"├" + dashLine + "┤\n" +
   162→		formatStr +
   163→		formatStr +
   164→		formatStr +
   165→		"└" + dashLine + "┘\n\n";
   166→
   167→	char buffer[640];
   168→	snprintf(buffer, sizeof(buffer),
   169→		headerStr.c_str(),
   170→		maxLen - 24, "",
   171→		networkInfo.c_str(),
   172→		passwordInfo.c_str(),
   173→		ipInfo.c_str()
   174→	);
   175→	Serial.print(buffer);
   176→}

  1093→// Utility to wrap meteor region if its out of bounds
  1094→uint8_t regionWrap(int8_t region, bool isDown)
  1095→{
  1096→	if (isDown) {
  1097→		if (region == outerChunks) return  0; // Wrap around to first strip, 1st pixel
  1098→		if (region == outerChunks + 1) return  1; // Wrap around to first strip, 2nd pixel
  1099→		if (region < 0) return outerChunks - 1; // Wrap around to last strip
  1100→	} else {
  1101→		if (region == middleChunks) return  0; // Wrap around to first strip, 1st pixel
  1102→		if (region == middleChunks + 1) return  1; // Wrap around to first strip, 2nd pixel
  1103→		if (region < 0) return middleChunks - 1; // Wrap around to last strip
  1104→	}
  1105→
  1106→	return region;
  1107→}

  1121→
  1122→	const uint16_t regionOffset = innerPixelsChunkLength * regionStart;

  1129→	for (int i = 0; i < ledCharacter.characterTotalPixels; i++) {

  1134→		int regionInt = (j % characterWidth) - 1;

  1138→		int drawPixel = (pixel + (innerPixelsChunkLength * regionInt)) % innerPixelsTotal;
  1139→		int drawPreviousPixel = (previousPixel + (innerPixelsChunkLength * regionInt)) % innerPixelsTotal;
  1140→
  1141→		int regionStart = (innerPixelsChunkLength * regionInt + regionOffset) % innerPixelsTotal;
  1142→		int regionEnd = (innerPixelsChunkLength * (regionInt + 1) + regionOffset) % innerPixelsTotal;

  1146→

  1174→void scrollLetters(const char* spacecraftName, int wordArraySize)

  1426→void zigzagAnimation(
  1427→	uint8_t strip,

  1431→	uint8_t pulseOffset,

  2037→const unsigned long ONE_Kbps = 1000;
  2038→const unsigned long TEN_Kbps = 10 * 1000;
  2039→const unsigned long FIFTY_Kbps = 50 * 1000;
  2040→const unsigned long HUNDRED_Kbps = 100 * 1000;
  2041→const unsigned long TWO_FIFTY_Kbps = 250 * 1000;
  2042→const unsigned long FIVE_HUNDRED_Kbps = 500 * 1000;
  2043→const unsigned long ONE_Mbps = 1000 * 1000;
  2044→const unsigned long TWO_Mbps = 2 * ONE_Mbps;
  2045→const unsigned long TWO_POINT_FIVE_Mbps = 2.5 * ONE_Mbps;
  2046→const unsigned long MAX_RATE = 1000 * ONE_Mbps; // 1 Gbps
  2047→
  2048→/* Convert long rate to rate class
  2049→ * Returns rate class as an unsigned int
  2050→ */
  2051→unsigned int rateLongToRateClass(unsigned long rate) {
  2052→	// Cap the rate at just above 10 Gbps to catch erroneous values
  2053→	unsigned long cappedRate = (rate > MAX_RATE) ? MAX_RATE : rate;
  2054→
  2055→	// Classify the rate into one of the 7 rate classes
  2056→	if (cappedRate == 0) return 0; // No Data
  2057→	else if (cappedRate < ONE_Kbps) return 1; // <1 Kbps
  2058→	else if (cappedRate < TEN_Kbps) return 2; // <50 Kbps
  2059→	else if (cappedRate < HUNDRED_Kbps) return 3; // <250 Kbps
  2060→	else if (cappedRate < FIVE_HUNDRED_Kbps) return 4; // <1 Mbps
  2061→	else if (cappedRate < TWO_POINT_FIVE_Mbps) return 5; // <2.5 Mbps
  2062→	else return 6; // 2.5 Mbps and above
  2063→}

   650→
   651→void printCurrentQueue(QueueHandle_t queue) {
   652→	char buffer[1024]; // Create a buffer to hold the serial output
   653→	snprintf(
   654→		buffer,
   655→		sizeof(buffer),
   656→		"\n%s========= QUEUE %d/%d ==========%s\n",
   657→		dev.termColor("purple"),
   658→		uxQueueMessagesWaiting(queue),
   659→		MAX_ITEMS,
   660→		dev.termColor("reset")
   661→	);
   662→
   663→	if (uxQueueMessagesWaiting(queue) > 0) {
   664→		QueueHandle_t tempQueue = xQueueCreate(5, sizeof(CraftQueueItem)); // Create a temporary queue to hold the items
   665→		if (tempQueue == NULL) {
   666→			Serial.println("Error: Could not create temporary queue.");
   667→			return;
   668→		}
   669→
   670→
   671→
   672→		CraftQueueItem theTempBuffer;
   673→		CraftQueueItem* tempBuffer = &theTempBuffer;
   674→
   675→		int queueCount = uxQueueMessagesWaiting(queue);
   676→		for (int i = 0; i < queueCount; i++) {
   677→			if (xQueueReceive(queue, &tempBuffer, (TickType_t)10)) {
   678→				String craftInfo = returnCraftInfo(i, tempBuffer->callsign, tempBuffer->name, tempBuffer->nameLength, tempBuffer->downSignal, tempBuffer->upSignal);
   679→				strncat(buffer, craftInfo.c_str(), sizeof(buffer) - strlen(buffer) - 1);
   680→
   681→				if (!xQueueSend(tempQueue, &tempBuffer, (TickType_t)10)) {
   682→					Serial.println("Error: Could not send data to the temporary queue.");
   683→					// Handle error as necessary, maybe break out of the loop
   684→				}
   685→			} else {
   686→				Serial.println("Error: Could not receive data from the main queue.");
   687→				break;
   688→			}
   689→		}
   690→
   691→		for (int i = 0; i < queueCount; i++) {
   692→			if (xQueueReceive(tempQueue, &tempBuffer, (TickType_t)10)) {
   693→				if (!xQueueSend(queue, &tempBuffer, (TickType_t)10)) {
   694→					Serial.println("Error: Could not send data back to the main queue.");
   695→					// Handle error as necessary, maybe break out of the loop
   696→				}
   697→			} else {
   698→				Serial.println("Error: Could not receive data from the temporary queue.");
   699→				// Handle error as necessary, maybe break out of the loop
   700→			}
   701→		}
   702→
   703→		vQueueDelete(tempQueue); // Delete the temporary queue
   704→	} else {
   705→		strncat(buffer, "Queue is empty.\n", sizeof(buffer) - strlen(buffer) - 1);
   706→	}
   707→
   708→	snprintf(buffer, sizeof(buffer), "%s%s===============================%s\n\n", buffer, dev.termColor("purple"), dev.termColor("reset"));
   709→	Serial.print(buffer);
   710→}

   722→void printSemaphoreList() {
   723→	// This function must be used inside a mutex lock
   724→	if (FileUtils::config.debugUtils.showSerial) {
   725→		Serial.print(
   726→			"\n=== freeListMutex [" +
   727→			String(freeListTop + 1) +
   728→			"/" +
   729→			String(MAX_ITEMS) +
   730→			"] ===\n");
   731→
   732→		for (int i = 0; i < MAX_ITEMS; i++) {
   733→			if (freeList[i] == nullptr) continue; // Skip null items
   734→
   735→			String marker = (i == freeListTop) ? ">" : " "; // Marker for top of freeList
   736→			Serial.print(
   737→				marker +
   738→				"[" +
   739→				String(i) +
   740→				"] " +
   741→				String(freeList[i]->callsignArray) +
   742→				"\n");
   743→		}
   744→		Serial.print("\n");
   745→	}
   746→}
   747→
   748→void freeSemaphoreItem(CraftQueueItem* infoBuffer) {
   749→	feedWatchdog();
   750→	if (xSemaphoreTake(freeListMutex, pdMS_TO_TICKS(500)) == pdTRUE) {
   751→
   752→		if (freeListTop < 0) {
   753→			Serial.println("Error: freeListTop is " + String(freeListTop) + "\n");
   754→			freeListTop = 0;
   755→		}
   756→
   757→		if (freeListTop > MAX_ITEMS - 1) {
   758→			Serial.println("Error: freeListTop is greater than MAX_ITEMS");
   759→			freeListTop = MAX_ITEMS - 1;
   760→		}
   761→
   762→		freeList[freeListTop] = infoBuffer;
   763→		freeListTop++;
   764→
   765→
   766→		char semaphoreStatusMessage[128];
   767→		snprintf(
   768→			semaphoreStatusMessage,
   769→			sizeof(semaphoreStatusMessage),
   770→			"%sSemaphore freed: %s [%d/%d]%s\n",
   771→			DevUtils::termColor("green"),
   772→			String(infoBuffer->callsignArray).c_str(),
   773→			freeListTop,
   774→			MAX_ITEMS,
   775→			DevUtils::termColor("reset")
   776→		);
   777→		infoBuffer = nullptr;
   778→
   779→		if (freeListMutex != nullptr) {
   780→			xSemaphoreGive(freeListMutex);
   781→		}
   782→	}
   783→}

  1785→	// Rate class update timing

  1788→		50, // Rate class 2
  1789→		40, // Rate class 3
  1790→		35, // Rate class 4
  1791→		20, // Rate class 5

  1803→	bool updateTable[6] = { false };
  1804→	bool spiralUpdateTable[6] = { false };

  1806→
  1807→	/* Update rate classes at different intervals */
  1808→	EVERY_N_MILLISECONDS(timingTable[0]) {

  1811→	EVERY_N_MILLISECONDS(timingTable[1]) {

  1823→	updateTable[5] = true; // Rate 6 is not slowed, it runs as fast as possible
  1824→
  1825→
  1826→	EVERY_N_MILLISECONDS(timingTable[0] * 4) {

  1829→	EVERY_N_MILLISECONDS(timingTable[1] * 4) {

  1859→	for (int i = 0; i < animate.ActiveMeteorArraySize; i++) {

  1862→			const int rateClass = thisMeteor->rateClass;

  1867→			if (debugMeasure) {

  1871→
  1872→
  1873→			/* Handline horizontal region changes */
  1874→			bool doSpiral = spiralUpdateTable[rateClass - 1];

  1876→
  1877→			if (shouldSpiral == true && doSpiral == true) {

  2037→const unsigned long ONE_Kbps = 1000;
  2038→const unsigned long TEN_Kbps = 10 * 1000;
  2039→const unsigned long FIFTY_Kbps = 50 * 1000;
  2040→const unsigned long HUNDRED_Kbps = 100 * 1000;
  2041→const unsigned long TWO_FIFTY_Kbps = 250 * 1000;
  2042→const unsigned long FIVE_HUNDRED_Kbps = 500 * 1000;
  2043→const unsigned long ONE_Mbps = 1000 * 1000;
  2044→const unsigned long TWO_Mbps = 2 * ONE_Mbps;
  2045→const unsigned long TWO_POINT_FIVE_Mbps = 2.5 * ONE_Mbps;
  2046→const unsigned long MAX_RATE = 1000 * ONE_Mbps; // 1 Gbps
  2047→
  2048→/* Convert long rate to rate class
  2049→ * Returns rate class as an unsigned int
  2050→ */
  2051→unsigned int rateLongToRateClass(unsigned long rate) {
  2052→	// Cap the rate at just above 10 Gbps to catch erroneous values
  2053→	unsigned long cappedRate = (rate > MAX_RATE) ? MAX_RATE : rate;
  2054→
  2055→	// Classify the rate into one of the 7 rate classes
  2056→	if (cappedRate == 0) return 0; // No Data
  2057→	else if (cappedRate < ONE_Kbps) return 1; // <1 Kbps
  2058→	else if (cappedRate < TEN_Kbps) return 2; // <50 Kbps
  2059→	else if (cappedRate < HUNDRED_Kbps) return 3; // <250 Kbps
  2060→	else if (cappedRate < FIVE_HUNDRED_Kbps) return 4; // <1 Mbps
  2061→	else if (cappedRate < TWO_POINT_FIVE_Mbps) return 5; // <2.5 Mbps
  2062→	else return 6; // 2.5 Mbps and above
  2063→}

  1093→// Utility to wrap meteor region if its out of bounds
  1094→uint8_t regionWrap(int8_t region, bool isDown)
  1095→{
  1096→	if (isDown) {
  1097→		if (region == outerChunks) return  0; // Wrap around to first strip, 1st pixel
  1098→		if (region == outerChunks + 1) return  1; // Wrap around to first strip, 2nd pixel
  1099→		if (region < 0) return outerChunks - 1; // Wrap around to last strip
  1100→	} else {
  1101→		if (region == middleChunks) return  0; // Wrap around to first strip, 1st pixel
  1102→		if (region == middleChunks + 1) return  1; // Wrap around to first strip, 2nd pixel
  1103→		if (region < 0) return middleChunks - 1; // Wrap around to last strip
  1104→	}
  1105→
  1106→	return region;
  1107→}

  1109→// Display letter from array
  1110→void doLetterRegions(char theLetter, int regionStart, int startingPixel)
  1111→{
  1112→	const TextCharacter::TextCharacterInfo ledCharacter = textCharacter.getCharacter(theLetter, characterWidth);
  1113→
  1114→	// Check if characterWidth is zero, if so, return from the function to avoid division by zero
  1115→	if (characterWidth == 0) {
  1116→		characterWidth = 5;
  1117→		Serial.println("Error: characterWidth is zero - setting to 5");
  1118→		// return;
  1119→	}
  1120→
  1121→
  1122→	const uint16_t regionOffset = innerPixelsChunkLength * regionStart;
  1123→
  1124→	int16_t pixel = startingPixel + regionOffset;
  1125→	const int16_t previousPixel = pixel - letterSpacing;
  1126→
  1127→	const size_t inner_leds_size = sizeof(inner_leds) / sizeof(inner_leds[0]);
  1128→
  1129→	for (int i = 0; i < ledCharacter.characterTotalPixels; i++) {
  1130→		int j = i + 1;
  1131→		// Serial.print("j: " + String(j) + "\n");
  1132→		// Serial.println("characterWidth: " + String(characterWidth) + "\n");
  1133→
  1134→		int regionInt = (j % characterWidth) - 1;
  1135→		if (regionInt < 0)
  1136→			regionInt = characterWidth - 1;
  1137→
  1138→		int drawPixel = (pixel + (innerPixelsChunkLength * regionInt)) % innerPixelsTotal;
  1139→		int drawPreviousPixel = (previousPixel + (innerPixelsChunkLength * regionInt)) % innerPixelsTotal;
  1140→
  1141→		int regionStart = (innerPixelsChunkLength * regionInt + regionOffset) % innerPixelsTotal;
  1142→		int regionEnd = (innerPixelsChunkLength * (regionInt + 1) + regionOffset) % innerPixelsTotal;
  1143→
  1144→		bool drawPixelInRegion = (regionStart <= drawPixel && drawPixel < regionEnd) ||
  1145→			(regionStart > regionEnd && (drawPixel < regionEnd || drawPixel >= regionStart));
  1146→
  1147→		bool drawPrevPixelInRegion = (regionStart <= drawPreviousPixel && drawPreviousPixel < regionEnd) ||
  1148→			(regionStart > regionEnd && (drawPreviousPixel < regionEnd || drawPreviousPixel >= regionStart));
  1149→
  1150→
  1151→		if (drawPrevPixelInRegion) {
  1152→			if (drawPreviousPixel >= 0 && drawPreviousPixel < inner_leds_size) {
  1153→				inner_leds[drawPreviousPixel] = mpColors.off.value;
  1154→			} else {
  1155→				// Serial.print(DevUtils::termColor("red")) + "drawPreviousPixel out of bounds" + DevUtils::termColor("reset")) + "\n");
  1156→			}
  1157→		}
  1158→
  1159→		if (drawPixelInRegion) {
  1160→			if (drawPixel >= 0 && drawPixel < inner_leds_size) {
  1161→				inner_leds[drawPixel] = ledCharacter.characterArray[i] == 1 ? currentColors.letter : mpColors.off.value;
  1162→			} else {
  1163→				// Serial.print(DevUtils::termColor("red")) + "drawPixel out of bounds" + DevUtils::termColor("reset")) + "\n");
  1164→			}
  1165→		}
  1166→
  1167→		if (regionInt == characterWidth - 1)
  1168→			pixel--;
  1169→	}
  1170→}

  1265→void animationMeteorPulseRegion(
  1266→	uint8_t strip,
  1267→	uint8_t region,
  1268→	bool directionDown = true,
  1269→	int16_t startPixel = 0,
  1270→	uint8_t pulseCount = 2,

  1273→	uint8_t meteorSize = 1,
  1274→	bool hasTail = true,

  1276→	int rateClass = 5,
  1277→	uint8_t animationType = 0
  1278→)
  1279→{
  1280→	// Stagger the starting pixel
  1281→	if (randomizeOffset == true)
  1282→		startPixel = startPixel - ((rand() % (offset / 2) + 1) * 2);
  1283→
  1284→	for (int i = 0; i < pulseCount; i++) {
  1285→		int16_t pixel = i + startPixel + (i * offset * -1);
  1286→		if (randomizeOffset == true)
  1287→			pixel = pixel - (random(0, 6) * 2);
  1288→		createMeteor(
  1289→			strip,
  1290→			region,
  1291→			directionDown,
  1292→			pixel,
  1293→			meteorSize,
  1294→			hasTail,
  1295→			meteorTailDecayValue,
  1296→			rateClass,
  1297→			animationType
  1298→		);
  1299→	}
  1300→}

  1333→void animationSpiralPulseRing(
  1334→	uint8_t strip,
  1335→	bool directionDown = true,
  1336→	uint8_t height = 2,
  1337→	uint8_t pulseCount = 2,
  1338→	uint8_t offset = 12,
  1339→	uint8_t spiralMultiplier = 6,
  1340→	uint8_t repeats = 4,
  1341→	bool hasTail = true,
  1342→	float meteorTailDecayValue = 0.93,

  1345→{
  1346→	for (int p = 0; p < pulseCount; p++) {
  1347→		for (int i = 0; i < outerChunks; i++) {
  1348→			int16_t startPixel = ((i * spiralMultiplier) + (p * offset)) * -1;
  1349→
  1350→			animationMeteorPulseRegion(
  1351→				strip,
  1352→				i,
  1353→				directionDown,
  1354→				startPixel,
  1355→				5,
  1356→				((outerChunks + 1) * spiralMultiplier),
  1357→				false,
  1358→				height,
  1359→				hasTail,
  1360→				meteorTailDecayValue,
  1361→				rateClass,
  1362→				animationType

  1368→
  1369→void waveAnimation(
  1370→	uint8_t strip,
  1371→	bool isDown,
  1372→	uint8_t numberOfWaves = 1,
  1373→	uint8_t offset = 12,
  1374→	uint8_t waveSize = 2,
  1375→	uint8_t interval = 4,
  1376→	bool hasTail = true,
  1377→	float meteorTailDecayValue = 0.93,
  1378→	int rateClass = 5,
  1379→	uint8_t animationType = 0)
  1380→{
  1381→	uint8_t intervalAdjusted = interval * 2; // Interval is doubled because the LEDs are in front/back pairs
  1382→	uint8_t startRegion;
  1383→
  1384→	if (isDown) {
  1385→		startRegion = random8(0, outerChunks);
  1386→	} else {
  1387→		startRegion = random8(0, middleChunks);
  1388→	}
  1389→
  1390→	for (uint8_t wave = 0; wave < numberOfWaves; wave++) {
  1391→		if (isDown) {
  1392→			startRegion += 2;
  1393→		} else {
  1394→			startRegion -= 2;
  1395→		}
  1396→
  1397→		startRegion = regionWrap(startRegion, isDown);
  1398→
  1399→		for (uint8_t region = 0; region < (isDown ? outerChunks : middleChunks); region++) {
  1400→			int startPixel = 0;
  1401→
  1402→			if (region < outerChunks / 2) {
  1403→				startPixel -= (intervalAdjusted * region) + (offset * wave);
  1404→			} else {
  1405→				startPixel -= (intervalAdjusted * (outerChunks - region)) + (offset * wave);
  1406→			}
  1407→
  1408→			createMeteor(
  1409→				strip,
  1410→				startRegion,
  1411→				isDown,
  1412→				startPixel,
  1413→				waveSize,
  1414→				hasTail,
  1415→				meteorTailDecayValue,
  1416→				rateClass,
  1417→				animationType
  1418→			);
  1419→
  1420→			startRegion++;
  1421→			startRegion = regionWrap(startRegion, isDown);
  1422→		}
  1423→	}
  1424→}

  1426→void zigzagAnimation(
  1427→	uint8_t strip,
  1428→	bool isDown,
  1429→	uint8_t pulseCount,
  1430→	uint8_t zigzagSize,
  1431→	uint8_t pulseOffset,
  1432→	uint8_t height,
  1433→	uint8_t interval,
  1434→	bool hasTail,
  1435→	float meteorTailDecayValue,
  1436→	int rateClass,
  1437→	uint8_t animationType = 0)
  1438→{
  1439→	zigzagSize--;
  1440→
  1441→	for (int pulse = 0; pulse < pulseCount; pulse++) {
  1442→		// Serial.print("pulse: " + String(pulse) + "\n");
  1443→
  1444→		for (uint8_t region = 0; region < outerChunks; region++) {
  1445→			// Serial.print("region: " + String(region) + "\n");
  1446→
  1447→			int startPixel;
  1448→			int position = region % (zigzagSize * 2);
  1449→
  1450→			if (position <= zigzagSize) {
  1451→				startPixel = (position * (interval * 2)) * -1;
  1452→			} else {
  1453→				startPixel = ((zigzagSize - (position - zigzagSize)) * (interval * 2)) * -1;
  1454→			}
  1455→
  1456→			/* Offset pulses */
  1457→			// pulseOffset is multiplied by 2 because the LEDs are in front/back pairs
  1458→			startPixel = startPixel - (pulse * (pulseOffset * 2));
  1459→
  1460→			// Serial.print("startPixel: " + String(startPixel) + "\n");
  1461→
  1462→			createMeteor(
  1463→				strip,
  1464→				region,
  1465→				isDown,
  1466→				startPixel,
  1467→				height,
  1468→				hasTail,
  1469→				meteorTailDecayValue,
  1470→				rateClass,
  1471→				animationType
  1472→			);
  1473→		}
  1474→	}
  1475→}

  1477→void laserGunAnimation(uint8_t strip, uint16_t chargeTime, uint8_t firingSize, int rateClass, uint8_t animationType = 0)
  1478→{
  1479→	// Charging up animation
  1480→	for (uint8_t i = 0; i < outerPixelsChunkLength; ++i) {
  1481→		for (uint8_t region = 0; region < outerChunks; ++region) {
  1482→			createMeteor(strip, region, true, i, 1, false, rateClass);
  1483→		}
  1484→		delay(chargeTime / outerPixelsChunkLength);
  1485→	}
  1486→
  1487→	// Firing animation
  1488→	for (uint8_t i = 0; i < outerPixelsChunkLength - firingSize + 1; ++i) {
  1489→		for (uint8_t region = 0; region < outerChunks; ++region) {
  1490→			createMeteor(strip, region, true, i, firingSize, true, rateClass);
  1491→		}
  1492→		delay(chargeTime / (outerPixelsChunkLength * 2));
  1493→	}
  1494→}

  1859→	for (int i = 0; i < animate.ActiveMeteorArraySize; i++) {
  1860→		if (animate.ActiveMeteors[i] != nullptr) {
  1861→			Meteor* thisMeteor = animate.ActiveMeteors[i];
  1862→			const int rateClass = thisMeteor->rateClass;
  1863→			const uint8_t animationType = thisMeteor->animationType;
  1864→			const int region = thisMeteor->region;
  1865→			const bool directionDown = thisMeteor->directionDown;
  1866→
  1867→			if (debugMeasure) {
  1868→				// Count the active meteors for diagnostic output
  1869→				activeMeteors++;
  1870→			}
  1871→
  1872→
  1873→			/* Handline horizontal region changes */
  1874→			bool doSpiral = spiralUpdateTable[rateClass - 1];
  1875→			bool shouldSpiral = animationTypeCanSpiralTable[animationType];
  1876→
  1877→			if (shouldSpiral == true && doSpiral == true) {
  1878→				int8_t newRegion = region;
  1879→				directionDown == true ? newRegion -= 1 : newRegion += 1; // Move meteor region based on direction
  1880→				newRegion = regionWrap(newRegion, directionDown); // Check for wrap around 
  1881→				thisMeteor->region = newRegion; // Update region in meteor object
  1882→			}
  1883→
  1884→			// Not ready to update meteor location, skip
  1885→			if (updateTable[rateClass - 1] == false) {
  1886→				continue;
  1887→			}
  1888→
  1889→
  1890→			// Update meteor location
  1891→			thisMeteor->firstPixel += 2; // Move meteor 2 pixels (visually moves by 1 due to back/front LED pairs)
  1892→
  1893→
  1894→			// When meteor reaches the end of the region, animate corresponding bottom pixel
  1895→			if (thisMeteor->firstPixel == thisMeteor->regionLength + 2 && thisMeteor->region % 2 == 1) {
  1896→				int bottomPixel = ((thisMeteor->region - 1) / 2) % 5;
  1897→				setBottomPixelToMax(bottomPixel);
  1898→			}
  1899→
  1900→			// If meteor is beyond the display region, unallocate memory and remove array item
  1901→			if (thisMeteor->firstPixel > thisMeteor->regionLength * 2) {
  1902→				delete thisMeteor;
  1903→				animate.ActiveMeteors[i] = nullptr;
  1904→			}
  1905→		}
  1906→	}
  1907→
  1908→	if (debugMeasure)
  1909→		Serial.print("Active_Meteors:" + String(activeMeteors) + ",");
  1910→}

  2037→const unsigned long ONE_Kbps = 1000;
  2038→const unsigned long TEN_Kbps = 10 * 1000;
  2039→const unsigned long FIFTY_Kbps = 50 * 1000;
  2040→const unsigned long HUNDRED_Kbps = 100 * 1000;
  2041→const unsigned long TWO_FIFTY_Kbps = 250 * 1000;
  2042→const unsigned long FIVE_HUNDRED_Kbps = 500 * 1000;
  2043→const unsigned long ONE_Mbps = 1000 * 1000;
  2044→const unsigned long TWO_Mbps = 2 * ONE_Mbps;
  2045→const unsigned long TWO_POINT_FIVE_Mbps = 2.5 * ONE_Mbps;
  2046→const unsigned long MAX_RATE = 1000 * ONE_Mbps; // 1 Gbps
  2047→
  2048→/* Convert long rate to rate class
  2049→ * Returns rate class as an unsigned int
  2050→ */
  2051→unsigned int rateLongToRateClass(unsigned long rate) {
  2052→	// Cap the rate at just above 10 Gbps to catch erroneous values
  2053→	unsigned long cappedRate = (rate > MAX_RATE) ? MAX_RATE : rate;
  2054→
  2055→	// Classify the rate into one of the 7 rate classes
  2056→	if (cappedRate == 0) return 0; // No Data
  2057→	else if (cappedRate < ONE_Kbps) return 1; // <1 Kbps
  2058→	else if (cappedRate < TEN_Kbps) return 2; // <50 Kbps
  2059→	else if (cappedRate < HUNDRED_Kbps) return 3; // <250 Kbps
  2060→	else if (cappedRate < FIVE_HUNDRED_Kbps) return 4; // <1 Mbps
  2061→	else if (cappedRate < TWO_POINT_FIVE_Mbps) return 5; // <2.5 Mbps
  2062→	else return 6; // 2.5 Mbps and above
  2063→}

  1652→
  1653→void doRateBasedAnimation(bool isDown, uint8_t rateClass, uint8_t offset, uint8_t type) {
  1654→	if (rateClass < 1 || rateClass > 6) return; // Invalid rate class
  1655→
  1656→	const bool showSerial = FileUtils::config.debugUtils.showSerial;
  1657→	const uint8_t stripId = isDown ? 2 : 1;
  1658→
  1659→
  1660→	// Serial.println("isDown: " + String(isDown) + " | strip: " + String(stripId) + " | rateClass: " + String(rateClass));
  1661→
  1662→
  1663→	// Determine animation type
  1664→	// uint8_t randomTypeAny = (rateClass <= 2) ? 0 : random8(0, 5);
  1665→	uint8_t randomTypeAny;
  1666→	// Serial.println("random roll: " + String(randomTypeAny));
  1667→
  1668→	if ((isDown && animateFirstCycleDown) || (!isDown && animateFirstCycleUp)) {
  1669→		if (rateClass == 5 || rateClass == 6) {
  1670→			randomTypeAny = random8(1, 5);
  1671→		} else if (rateClass == 3 || rateClass == 4) {
  1672→			randomTypeAny = 0;
  1673→		}
  1674→	} else if (rateClass == 5 || rateClass == 6) {
  1675→		randomTypeAny = random8(0, 5);
  1676→	} else if (rateClass == 4) {
  1677→		randomTypeAny = random8(0, 4);
  1678→	} else if (rateClass == 3) {
  1679→		randomTypeAny = random8(0, 3);
  1680→	} else {
  1681→		randomTypeAny = 0;
  1682→	}
  1683→
  1684→	if (animate.forcedAnimationType > 0)
  1685→		randomTypeAny = animate.forcedAnimationType - 1;
  1686→
  1687→	// Debug log
  1688→	if (showSerial) {
  1689→		const char* direction = isDown ? "(↓)" : "(↑)";
  1690→		char buffer[256];
  1691→
  1692→		snprintf(
  1693→			buffer,
  1694→			sizeof(buffer),
  1695→			"%s·.·.·.·.·.·★ %s Rate Class: %d | Type: %d\n",
  1696→			DevUtils::termColor("cyan"),
  1697→			direction,
  1698→			rateClass,
  1699→			randomTypeAny,
  1700→			DevUtils::termColor("reset")
  1701→		);
  1702→		Serial.print(buffer);
  1703→	}
  1704→
  1705→	// Lookup settings
  1706→	const RateClassSettings* currentRateSettings = rateClassSettings[rateClass - 1];
  1707→
  1708→	/* Assign animation types */
  1709→	if (currentRateSettings) {
  1710→		const RateClassSettings& settings = currentRateSettings[randomTypeAny];
  1711→
  1712→		if (rateClass == 1) {
  1713→			// Only one meteor for down and one for up
  1714→			animationMeteorPulseRegion(stripId, random8(0, 11), isDown, 0, settings.pulseCount, settings.offset, settings.randomizeOffset, settings.meteorSize, settings.hasTail, settings.meteorTailDecayValue, rateClass, randomTypeAny);
  1715→		} else {
  1716→			switch (randomTypeAny) {
  1717→				case 0:
  1718→				case 1:
  1719→					animationMeteorPulseRing(stripId, isDown, settings.pulseCount, settings.offset, settings.randomizeOffset, settings.meteorSize, settings.hasTail, settings.meteorTailDecayValue, rateClass, randomTypeAny);
  1720→					break;
  1721→				case 2:
  1722→					animationSpiralPulseRing(stripId, isDown, settings.height, settings.pulseCount, settings.offset, settings.spiralMultiplier, settings.repeats, settings.hasTail, settings.meteorTailDecayValue, rateClass, randomTypeAny);
  1723→					break;
  1724→				case 3:
  1725→					waveAnimation(stripId, isDown, settings.numberOfWaves, settings.offset, settings.waveSize, settings.interval, settings.hasTail, settings.meteorTailDecayValue, rateClass, randomTypeAny);
  1726→					break;
  1727→				case 4:
  1728→					zigzagAnimation(stripId, isDown, settings.pulseCount, settings.zigzagSize, settings.offset, settings.height, settings.interval, settings.hasTail, settings.meteorTailDecayValue, rateClass, randomTypeAny);
  1729→					break;
  1730→			}
  1731→		}
  1732→	}
  1733→
  1734→
  1735→	const InnerCoreMeteorSettings& ics = innerCoreSettings[rateClass - 1];
  1736→
  1737→	// Inner Core meteors
  1738→	if (isDown) {
  1739→		// doInnerCoreMeteors(true, ics.pulseCount, ics.offset, ics.meteorCount, ics.meteorTailDecayValue, rateClass);
  1740→
  1741→		// Inlined doCoreMeteors() here for performance		
  1742→		for (uint8_t i = 0; i < ics.meteorCount; i++) {
  1743→			animationMeteorPulseRegion(0, random8(4, 9), isDown, 0, ics.pulseCount, offset, true, 1, true, ics.meteorTailDecayValue, rateClass);
  1744→		}
  1745→
  1746→		animateFirstCycleDown = false;
  1747→	} else {
  1748→		animateFirstCycleUp = false;
  1749→	}
  1750→}

  1781→void updateMeteors()
  1782→{
  1783→	bool debugMeasure = FileUtils::config.debugUtils.diagMeasure;
  1784→
  1785→	// Rate class update timing
  1786→	int8_t timingTable[6] = {
  1787→		60, // Rate class 1
  1788→		50, // Rate class 2
  1789→		40, // Rate class 3
  1790→		35, // Rate class 4
  1791→		20, // Rate class 5
  1792→		10  // Rate class 6
  1793→	};
  1794→
  1795→	bool animationTypeCanSpiralTable[5] = {
  1796→		false,
  1797→		false,
  1798→		false,
  1799→		true,
  1800→		false,
  1801→	};
  1802→
  1803→	bool updateTable[6] = { false };
  1804→	bool spiralUpdateTable[6] = { false };
  1805→
  1806→
  1807→	/* Update rate classes at different intervals */
  1808→	EVERY_N_MILLISECONDS(timingTable[0]) {
  1809→		updateTable[0] = true; // Rate class 1
  1810→	}
  1811→	EVERY_N_MILLISECONDS(timingTable[1]) {
  1812→		updateTable[1] = true; // Rate class 2
  1813→	}
  1814→	EVERY_N_MILLISECONDS(timingTable[2]) {
  1815→		updateTable[2] = true; // Rate class 3
  1816→	}
  1817→	EVERY_N_MILLISECONDS(timingTable[3]) {
  1818→		updateTable[3] = true; // Rate class 4
  1819→	}
  1820→	EVERY_N_MILLISECONDS(timingTable[4]) {
  1821→		updateTable[4] = true; // Rate class 5
  1822→	}
  1823→	updateTable[5] = true; // Rate 6 is not slowed, it runs as fast as possible
  1824→
  1825→
  1826→	EVERY_N_MILLISECONDS(timingTable[0] * 4) {
  1827→		spiralUpdateTable[0] = true;
  1828→	}
  1829→	EVERY_N_MILLISECONDS(timingTable[1] * 4) {
  1830→		spiralUpdateTable[1] = true;
  1831→	}
  1832→	EVERY_N_MILLISECONDS(timingTable[2] * 4) {
  1833→		spiralUpdateTable[2] = true;
  1834→	}
  1835→	EVERY_N_MILLISECONDS(timingTable[3] * 4) {
  1836→		spiralUpdateTable[3] = true;
  1837→	}
  1838→	EVERY_N_MILLISECONDS(timingTable[4] * 4) {
  1839→		spiralUpdateTable[4] = true;
  1840→	}
  1841→	EVERY_N_MILLISECONDS(timingTable[5] * 4) {
  1842→		spiralUpdateTable[5] = true;
  1843→	}
  1844→
  1845→
  1846→
  1847→
  1848→	// // Print the updateTable array
  1849→	// Serial.print("updateTable: ");
  1850→	// for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++) {
  1851→	// 	Serial.print("[" + String(updateTable[i]) + "]");
  1852→	// }
  1853→	// Serial.print("\n");
  1854→
  1855→
  1856→	// Update first pixel location for all active Meteors in array
  1857→	uint16_t activeMeteors = 0;
  1858→
  1859→	for (int i = 0; i < animate.ActiveMeteorArraySize; i++) {
  1860→		if (animate.ActiveMeteors[i] != nullptr) {
  1861→			Meteor* thisMeteor = animate.ActiveMeteors[i];
  1862→			const int rateClass = thisMeteor->rateClass;
  1863→			const uint8_t animationType = thisMeteor->animationType;
  1864→			const int region = thisMeteor->region;
  1865→			const bool directionDown = thisMeteor->directionDown;
  1866→
  1867→			if (debugMeasure) {
  1868→				// Count the active meteors for diagnostic output
  1869→				activeMeteors++;
  1870→			}
  1871→
  1872→
  1873→			/* Handline horizontal region changes */
  1874→			bool doSpiral = spiralUpdateTable[rateClass - 1];
  1875→			bool shouldSpiral = animationTypeCanSpiralTable[animationType];
  1876→
  1877→			if (shouldSpiral == true && doSpiral == true) {
  1878→				int8_t newRegion = region;
  1879→				directionDown == true ? newRegion -= 1 : newRegion += 1; // Move meteor region based on direction
  1880→				newRegion = regionWrap(newRegion, directionDown); // Check for wrap around 
  1881→				thisMeteor->region = newRegion; // Update region in meteor object
  1882→			}
  1883→
  1884→			// Not ready to update meteor location, skip
  1885→			if (updateTable[rateClass - 1] == false) {
  1886→				continue;
  1887→			}
  1888→
  1889→
  1890→			// Update meteor location
  1891→			thisMeteor->firstPixel += 2; // Move meteor 2 pixels (visually moves by 1 due to back/front LED pairs)
  1892→
  1893→
  1894→			// When meteor reaches the end of the region, animate corresponding bottom pixel
  1895→			if (thisMeteor->firstPixel == thisMeteor->regionLength + 2 && thisMeteor->region % 2 == 1) {
  1896→				int bottomPixel = ((thisMeteor->region - 1) / 2) % 5;
  1897→				setBottomPixelToMax(bottomPixel);
  1898→			}
  1899→
  1900→			// If meteor is beyond the display region, unallocate memory and remove array item
  1901→			if (thisMeteor->firstPixel > thisMeteor->regionLength * 2) {
  1902→				delete thisMeteor;
  1903→				animate.ActiveMeteors[i] = nullptr;
  1904→			}
  1905→		}
  1906→	}
  1907→
  1908→	if (debugMeasure)
  1909→		Serial.print("Active_Meteors:" + String(activeMeteors) + ",");
  1910→}

  2781→void logOutput(const char* color, const String& message) {
  2782→	const bool showSerial = FileUtils::config.debugUtils.showSerial;
  2783→	if (showSerial == true) {
  2784→		String resetColorString = DevUtils::termColor("reset");
  2785→		String coloredMessageString = DevUtils::termColor(color);
  2786→
  2787→		const char* resetColor = resetColorString.c_str();
  2788→		const char* coloredMessage = coloredMessageString.c_str();
  2789→
  2790→		int bufferSize = strlen(coloredMessage) + message.length() + strlen(resetColor) + 2; // +1 for newline, +1 for null terminator
  2791→
  2792→		const char* messageCharPtr = message.c_str();
  2793→
  2794→		char* buffer = (char*)malloc(bufferSize);
  2795→		if (buffer) {
  2796→			snprintf(
  2797→				buffer,
  2798→				bufferSize,
  2799→				"%s%s%s\n",
  2800→				coloredMessage,
  2801→				messageCharPtr,
  2802→				resetColor
  2803→			);
  2804→			Serial.print(buffer);
  2805→			free(buffer);
  2806→		} else {
  2807→			// handle memory allocation failure
  2808→			if (showSerial == true)
  2809→				Serial.print("Memory allocation failed\n");
  2810→		}
  2811→	}
  2812→}

  2781→void logOutput(const char* color, const String& message) {
  2782→	const bool showSerial = FileUtils::config.debugUtils.showSerial;
  2783→	if (showSerial == true) {
  2784→		String resetColorString = DevUtils::termColor("reset");
  2785→		String coloredMessageString = DevUtils::termColor(color);
  2786→
  2787→		const char* resetColor = resetColorString.c_str();
  2788→		const char* coloredMessage = coloredMessageString.c_str();
  2789→
  2790→		int bufferSize = strlen(coloredMessage) + message.length() + strlen(resetColor) + 2; // +1 for newline, +1 for null terminator
  2791→
  2792→		const char* messageCharPtr = message.c_str();
  2793→
  2794→		char* buffer = (char*)malloc(bufferSize);
  2795→		if (buffer) {
  2796→			snprintf(
  2797→				buffer,
  2798→				bufferSize,
  2799→				"%s%s%s\n",
  2800→				coloredMessage,
  2801→				messageCharPtr,
  2802→				resetColor
  2803→			);
  2804→			Serial.print(buffer);
  2805→			free(buffer);
  2806→		} else {
  2807→			// handle memory allocation failure
  2808→			if (showSerial == true)
  2809→				Serial.print("Memory allocation failed\n");
  2810→		}
  2811→	}
  2812→}

  2865→bool attemptHTTPConnection(const String& url) {
  2866→	if (!http.begin(url.c_str())) {
  2867→		logOutput("red", "[!] Failed to connect to server");
  2868→		return false;
  2869→	}
  2870→	feedWatchdog();
  2871→	http.setTimeout(5000);
  2872→	http.addHeader("Content-Type", "text/xml");
  2873→	int httpResponseCode = http.GET();
  2874→	feedWatchdog();
  2875→	return handleHttpResponse(httpResponseCode);
  2876→}

  2878→bool fetchHTTPData(const String& url) {
  2879→	bool showSerial = FileUtils::config.debugUtils.showSerial;
  2880→
  2881→	const int maxHttpRetries = 3;
  2882→	for (int retry = 0; retry < maxHttpRetries; retry++) {
  2883→		feedWatchdog(); // HTTP connection can sometimes be slow
  2884→
  2885→		char conectionAttemptBuffer[128];
  2886→		snprintf(
  2887→			conectionAttemptBuffer,
  2888→			sizeof(conectionAttemptBuffer),
  2889→			"%sHTTP connection attempt %d of %d%s\n",
  2890→			DevUtils::termColor("yellow"),
  2891→			retry + 1,
  2892→			maxHttpRetries,
  2893→			DevUtils::termColor("reset")
  2894→		);
  2895→
  2896→		try {
  2897→			if (attemptHTTPConnection(url) == true) {
  2898→				if (showSerial) {
  2899→					Serial.print("Getting string from API response...\n");
  2900→				}
  2901→
  2902→				try {
  2903→					String res = http.getString();
  2904→
  2905→					if (res == nullptr or res.length() == 0 or res == "") {
  2906→						Serial.print("Error: API response is empty\n");
  2907→						http.end();
  2908→						return false;
  2909→					}
  2910→
  2911→					feedWatchdog(); // The response may be large, just in case
  2912→
  2913→					if (showSerial) {
  2914→						Serial.print("Writing XML data to file...\n");
  2915→					}
  2916→
  2917→					File xmlFile = LittleFS.open("/temp.xml", "w");
  2918→					if (!xmlFile) {
  2919→						logOutput("red", "Failed to open XML file for writing");
  2920→						http.end();
  2921→						return false;
  2922→					}
  2923→
  2924→					size_t bytesWritten = xmlFile.print(res);
  2925→					xmlFile.close();
  2926→					feedWatchdog(); // Just in case writing to the file is slow
  2927→				}
  2928→				catch (...) {
  2929→					Serial.print("Error getting string from API response\n");
  2930→				}
  2931→
  2932→				http.end();
  2933→				return true; // XML data saved to LittleFS
  2934→			} else {
  2935→				http.end();
  2936→				if (FileUtils::config.debugUtils.showSerial == true)
  2937→					Serial.println("[fetchHTTPData] Failed to fetch data");
  2938→			}
  2939→
  2940→			// vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(100)); // Wait to allow other tasks to run
  2941→		}
  2942→		catch (...) {
  2943→			Serial.println("Error: fetchHTTPData() failed");
  2944→			dev.handleException();
  2945→			http.end();  // Close connection in case of an exception
  2946→			vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(100)); // Replace delay with vTaskDelay
  2947→		}
  2948→	}
  2949→	http.end();  // Ensure connection is closed even if no successful fetch
  2950→	return false;  // No data fetched
  2951→}

    15→    Serial.println("Loading spacecraft blacklist...");
    16→    SpacecraftData::loadSpacecraftBlacklistFile();
    17→    delay(100);
    18→    Serial.println("Loading spacecraft placeholder rates...");
    19→    SpacecraftData::loadSpacecraftPlaceholderRatesFile();
    20→    delay(100);
    21→};

   154→// Load spacecraft Names
   155→void SpacecraftData::loadSpacecraftNamesFile()
   156→{
   157→    SpacecraftData::createAndWriteNamesFile();
   158→
   159→    Serial.println("Loading spacecraft names from filesystem...");
   160→
   161→    FileUtils::createDir("spacecraft_data");
   162→
   163→    // Open file for reading
   164→    Serial.println("Opening names.json for reading...");
   165→    File file = LittleFS.open("/spacecraft_data/names.json", "r");
   166→
   167→    if (!file) {
   168→        Serial.print(DevUtils::termColor("red") + "Failed trying to open names.json" + DevUtils::termColor("reset") + "\n");
   169→        return;
   170→    }
   171→
   172→    Serial.println("File \"names.json\" opened successfully");
   173→
   174→    size_t size = file.size();
   175→    if (size > 5120) {
   176→        Serial.print(DevUtils::termColor("red") + "names.json file size is too large" + DevUtils::termColor("reset") + "\n");
   177→        return;
   178→    }
   179→
   180→    Serial.println("Deserializing JSON from file...");
   181→    DeserializationError error = deserializeJson(spacecraftNamesJson, file);
   182→    file.close();
   183→    vTaskDelay(100); // Make sure the file is closed
   184→
   185→    if (error) {
   186→        Serial.print(DevUtils::termColor("red") + "Failed trying to deserialize names JSON with error: " + error.c_str() + DevUtils::termColor("reset") + "\n");
   187→        return;
   188→    }
   189→
   190→    Serial.print(DevUtils::termColor("green") + "Spacecraft names loaded" + DevUtils::termColor("reset") + "\n");
   191→    // Serial.print("\n");
   192→}

   205→        return;
   206→    }
   207→
   208→    // Prep JSON buffer

   235→void SpacecraftData::loadSpacecraftBlacklistFile() {
   236→    SpacecraftData::createAndWriteBlacklistFile();
   237→    
   238→    Serial.println("Loading spacecraft blacklist from filesystem...");
   239→    
   240→    FileUtils::createDir("spacecraft_data");
   241→    
   242→
   243→    // Open file for reading
   244→    Serial.println("Opening blacklist.json for reading...");
   245→    File file = LittleFS.open("/spacecraft_data/blacklist.json", "r");
   246→
   247→    if (!file) {
   248→        Serial.print(DevUtils::termColor("red") + "Failed trying to open blacklist.json" + DevUtils::termColor("reset") + "\n");
   249→        return;
   250→    }
   251→
   252→    Serial.println("File \"blacklist.json\" opened successfully");
   253→
   254→    size_t size = file.size();
   255→    if (size > 1024) {
   256→        Serial.print(DevUtils::termColor("red") + "blacklist.json file size is too large" + DevUtils::termColor("reset") + "\n");
   257→        return;
   258→    }
   259→
   260→    Serial.println("Deserializing JSON...");
   261→    DeserializationError error = deserializeJson(spacecraftBlacklistJson, file);
   262→    file.close();
   263→
   264→    if (error) {
   265→        if (FileUtils::config.debugUtils.showSerial)
   266→            Serial.print(DevUtils::termColor("red") + "Failed trying to deserialize blacklist.json with error: " + error.c_str() + DevUtils::termColor("reset") + "\n");
   267→
   268→        return;
   269→    }
   270→
   271→    Serial.print(DevUtils::termColor("green") + "Spacecraft blacklist loaded" + DevUtils::termColor("reset") + "\n");
   272→    Serial.print("\n\n");
   273→}

    13→void Animate::animateMeteor(Meteor* meteor)
    14→{
    15→	// Set variables from meteor struct
    16→	CRGB* strip = meteor->rStrip;
    17→	int region = meteor->region;
    18→	int regionLength = meteor->regionLength;
    19→	CHSV pColor = meteor->pColor;
    20→	int meteorSize = meteor->meteorSize;
    21→	bool hasTail = meteor->hasTail;
    22→	bool meteorRandomDecay = meteor->meteorRandomDecay;
    23→	int tailHueStart = meteor->tailHueStart;
    24→	bool tailHueAdd = meteor->tailHueAdd;
    25→	double tailHueExponent = meteor->tailHueExponent;
    26→	int tailHueSaturation = meteor->tailHueSaturation;
    27→	int beginPixel = meteor->firstPixel;
    28→
    29→	CHSV pRepeatColor = pColor; // Initalize repeat color to meteor color
    30→	int hue = tailHueStart;
    31→
    32→	// Calculations are multiplied by two for pixel doubling on frontside/backside LED pairs on stick
    33→
    34→	// Calculate tail length
    35→	int tailStartBrightness = tailBrightnessMap[0];
    36→	int tailBrightnessMax = tailStartBrightness + 8;
    37→	int tailLength = tailBrightnessMapLength;
    38→	int tailSection = tailStartBrightness / tailLength;
    39→	int halfTailSection = tailSection * 0.5;
    40→	int adjustedLength = ((meteorSize + tailLength) * 2); // Length of animation for both sides of LED strip
    41→
    42→	// First pixel of each region
    43→	int startPixel = meteor->directionDown == true ?
    44→		((region + 1) * regionLength) - 1 : startPixel = region * regionLength;
    45→
    46→	// Current pixel to draw
    47→	int drawPixel = meteor->directionDown == true
    48→		? startPixel - beginPixel
    49→		: drawPixel = startPixel + beginPixel;
    50→
    51→	// Calculate region start and end
    52→	int regionStart = regionLength * region; // Calculate the pixel before the region start
    53→	int regionEnd = (regionLength * (region + 1) - 1); // Calculate the pixel after the region end
    54→
    55→	bool endTail = false; // Flag to end tail
    56→
    57→
    58→	// Draw every LED based on meteor size and tail length
    59→	for (int d = 1; d < (adjustedLength) + 2; d++) {
    60→		
    61→		// Set current pixel to draw
    62→		int currentPixel;
    63→		if (meteor->directionDown == true) {
    64→			currentPixel = drawPixel + d + 1;
    65→			if (currentPixel > regionEnd) break;
    66→			if (currentPixel < regionStart) continue;
    67→		} else {
    68→			currentPixel = drawPixel - d - 1;
    69→			if (currentPixel < regionStart) break;
    70→			if (currentPixel > regionEnd) continue;
    71→		}
    72→
    73→		// Draw backside LED
    74→		if (d - 1 % 2 == 0) {
    75→			strip[currentPixel] = pRepeatColor; // Set pixel to match frontside LED
    76→			continue;
    77→		}
    78→
    79→		// Draw meteor core
    80→		if (d < (meteorSize * 2) + 1) {
    81→			strip[currentPixel] = pColor; // Set pixel color
    82→			continue;
    83→		}
    84→
    85→		// No tail, so turn off pixel
    86→		if (hasTail == false) {
    87→			if (d > (meteorSize * 2) - 1) {
    88→				strip[currentPixel] = CHSV(0, 0, 0);
    89→				continue;
    90→			}
    91→		}
    92→
    93→		// If end tail has been flagged, end the loop
    94→		if (endTail == true) {
    95→			strip[currentPixel] = CHSV(0, 0, 0); // Turn off pixel
    96→			break;
    97→		}
    98→
    99→		// Set tail brightness
   100→		int tailBrightness;
   101→		if (d < 0 || d > (tailBrightnessMapLength * 2) - 1) {
   102→			// This LED is out of bounds, turn off pixel
   103→			strip[currentPixel] = CHSV(0, 0, 0);
   104→			continue;
   105→		} else {
   106→			// Look up tail brightness from map
   107→			tailBrightness = d % 2 == 1
   108→				? tailBrightnessMap[(d - 1) / 2] // This LED is odd
   109→				: tailBrightnessMap[d / 2]; // This LED is even
   110→		}
   111→
   112→		
   113→		if (meteorRandomDecay == true) {
   114→			// Calculate random variance
   115→			uint8_t tailNumberVarianceCalc = (d + 2) * 4;
   116→			tailBrightness += random8(tailNumberVarianceCalc) - (tailNumberVarianceCalc - 8);
   117→		}
   118→
   119→		// Clamp brightness to 8-190 via min/max
   120→		uint8_t brightValue = std::min((int)tailBrightnessMax, std::max(8, (int)tailBrightness));
   121→		
   122→		// Turn off tail after tailSectionLength pixels
   123→		if (d > (tailBrightnessMapLength * 2) + 4) brightValue = 0;
   124→
   125→		// Adjust brightness for gamma correction
   126→		uint8_t brightCalc = dim8_video(brightValue); // dim8_video floor is 1
   127→
   128→		// Create tail color color object
   129→		CHSV tailColor = CHSV(hue, tailHueSaturation, brightCalc);
   130→
   131→
   132→		// Make sure the pixel right after the meteor will get drawn so meteor values aren't repeated
   133→		if (d < (meteorSize + 1)) {
   134→			strip[currentPixel] = tailColor;
   135→			continue;
   136→		}
   137→
   138→		strip[currentPixel] = tailColor;
   139→
   140→		pRepeatColor = tailColor;

   142→		if (brightValue == 0) {
   143→			// endTail = true;
   144→			continue;
   145→		}
   146→
   147→		// if (brightValue == 0) endTail == true;
   148→	
   149→	} // End for loop
   150→}

    54→

    56→
    57→
    58→	// Draw every LED based on meteor size and tail length
    59→	for (int d = 1; d < (adjustedLength) + 2; d++) {
    60→		
    61→		// Set current pixel to draw
    62→		int currentPixel;
    63→		if (meteor->directionDown == true) {
    64→			currentPixel = drawPixel + d + 1;
    65→			if (currentPixel > regionEnd) break;
    66→			if (currentPixel < regionStart) continue;
    67→		} else {
    68→			currentPixel = drawPixel - d - 1;
    69→			if (currentPixel < regionStart) break;
    70→			if (currentPixel > regionEnd) continue;
    71→		}
    72→
    73→		// Draw backside LED
    74→		if (d - 1 % 2 == 0) {
    75→			strip[currentPixel] = pRepeatColor; // Set pixel to match frontside LED
    76→			continue;
    77→		}
    78→
    79→		// Draw meteor core
    80→		if (d < (meteorSize * 2) + 1) {
    81→			strip[currentPixel] = pColor; // Set pixel color
    82→			continue;
    83→		}
    84→
    85→		// No tail, so turn off pixel
    86→		if (hasTail == false) {
    87→			if (d > (meteorSize * 2) - 1) {
    88→				strip[currentPixel] = CHSV(0, 0, 0);
    89→				continue;
    90→			}
    91→		}
    92→
    93→		// If end tail has been flagged, end the loop
    94→		if (endTail == true) {
    95→			strip[currentPixel] = CHSV(0, 0, 0); // Turn off pixel
    96→			break;
    97→		}
    98→
    99→		// Set tail brightness
   100→		int tailBrightness;
   101→		if (d < 0 || d > (tailBrightnessMapLength * 2) - 1) {
   102→			// This LED is out of bounds, turn off pixel
   103→			strip[currentPixel] = CHSV(0, 0, 0);
   104→			continue;
   105→		} else {
   106→			// Look up tail brightness from map
   107→			tailBrightness = d % 2 == 1
   108→				? tailBrightnessMap[(d - 1) / 2] // This LED is odd
   109→				: tailBrightnessMap[d / 2]; // This LED is even
   110→		}
   111→
   112→		
   113→		if (meteorRandomDecay == true) {
   114→			// Calculate random variance
   115→			uint8_t tailNumberVarianceCalc = (d + 2) * 4;
   116→			tailBrightness += random8(tailNumberVarianceCalc) - (tailNumberVarianceCalc - 8);
   117→		}
   118→
   119→		// Clamp brightness to 8-190 via min/max
   120→		uint8_t brightValue = std::min((int)tailBrightnessMax, std::max(8, (int)tailBrightness));
   121→		
   122→		// Turn off tail after tailSectionLength pixels
   123→		if (d > (tailBrightnessMapLength * 2) + 4) brightValue = 0;
   124→
   125→		// Adjust brightness for gamma correction
   126→		uint8_t brightCalc = dim8_video(brightValue); // dim8_video floor is 1
   127→
   128→		// Create tail color color object
   129→		CHSV tailColor = CHSV(hue, tailHueSaturation, brightCalc);
   130→
   131→
   132→		// Make sure the pixel right after the meteor will get drawn so meteor values aren't repeated
   133→		if (d < (meteorSize + 1)) {
   134→			strip[currentPixel] = tailColor;
   135→			continue;
   136→		}
   137→
   138→		strip[currentPixel] = tailColor;
   139→
   140→		pRepeatColor = tailColor;
   141→
   142→		if (brightValue == 0) {
   143→			// endTail = true;
   144→			continue;
   145→		}
   146→
   147→		// if (brightValue == 0) endTail == true;
   148→	
   149→	} // End for loop
   150→}

   506→/**
   507→ * Spacecraft Placeholder Rates
   508→ */
   509→void SpacecraftData::loadSpacecraftPlaceholderRatesFile() {
   510→
   511→    SpacecraftData::createAndWritePlaceholderRatesFile();
   512→
   513→    Serial.println("Loading spacecraft placeholder rates from filesystem...");
   514→    Serial.println("Free Heap: " + String(ESP.getFreeHeap()));
   515→
   516→    // Check & create spacecraft_data directory
   517→    if (!LittleFS.exists("/spacecraft_data")) {
   518→        LittleFS.mkdir("/spacecraft_data");
   519→
   520→        if (!LittleFS.exists("/spacecraft_data")) {
   521→            Serial.print(DevUtils::termColor("red") + "Failed trying to create spacecraft_data directory" + DevUtils::termColor("reset") + "\n");
   522→            return;
   523→        }
   524→    }
   525→
   526→    // Open file for reading
   527→    File jsonFile = LittleFS.open("/spacecraft_data/placeholder_rates.json", "r");
   528→
   529→    if (!jsonFile) {
   530→        Serial.print(DevUtils::termColor("red") + "Failed trying to open placeholder_rates.json with error: " + DevUtils::termColor("reset") + "\n");
   531→        return;
   532→    }
   533→
   534→    Serial.println("File \"placeholder_rates.json\" opened");
   535→    Serial.println("Free Heap: " + String(ESP.getFreeHeap()));
   536→
   537→    size_t fileSize = jsonFile.size();
   538→    if (fileSize > 6144) {
   539→        Serial.print(DevUtils::termColor("red") + "placeholder_rates.json is too large" + DevUtils::termColor("reset") + "\n");
   540→        return;
   541→    }
   542→
   543→    DeserializationError error = deserializeJson(spacecraftPlaceholderRatesJson, jsonFile);
   544→    jsonFile.close();
   545→
   546→    if (error) {
   547→        Serial.print(DevUtils::termColor("red") + "Failed trying to deserialize placeholder_rates.json with error: " + error.c_str() + DevUtils::termColor("reset") + "\n");
   548→        return;
   549→    }
   550→    Serial.print(DevUtils::termColor("green") + "Spacecraft placeholder rates loaded" + DevUtils::termColor("reset") + "\n");
   551→    Serial.print("\n\n");
   552→}

   613→/* Check Blacklist */
   614→bool SpacecraftData::checkBlacklist(const char* key) {
   615→    bool showSerial = FileUtils::config.debugUtils.showSerial;
   616→    bool isBlacklisted = spacecraftBlacklistJson[key] != nullptr; // If the key is not null, it is blacklisted
   617→
   618→    if (showSerial) {
   619→        char buffer[128]; // Size this appropriately for your expected output length
   620→        // const char* isBlacklistedString = isBlacklisted ? "TRUE" : "FALSE";
   621→
   622→        if (isBlacklisted) {
   623→            snprintf(
   624→                buffer,
   625→                sizeof(buffer),
   626→                "%s%s is blacklisted, skipping...%s\n", 
   627→                DevUtils::termColor("purple"), 
   628→                key, 
   629→                DevUtils::termColor("reset")
   630→            );
   631→            Serial.print(buffer);
   632→        }
   633→    }
   634→
   635→    return isBlacklisted;
   636→}

   639→/* Get placeholder rate */
   640→const char* SpacecraftData::getPlaceholderRate(const char* key) {
   641→
   642→    bool showSerial = FileUtils::config.debugUtils.showSerial;
   643→
   644→    // Look for key in JSON
   645→    // File jsonFile = LittleFS.open("/spacecraft_data/placeholder_rates.json", "r");
   646→
   647→    // if (showSerial) {
   648→    //     if (jsonFile) {
   649→    //         Serial.println("File \"placeholder_rates.json\" opened");
   650→    //     } else {
   651→    //         Serial.println(DevUtils::termColor("red") + "Failed to open placeholder_rates.json" + DevUtils::termColor("reset") + "\n");
   652→    //     }
   653→    // }
   654→
   655→    // // put jsonFile into jsonBuffer
   656→    // DeserializationError error = deserializeJson(spacecraftPlaceholderRatesJson, jsonFile);
   657→    // // jsonFile.close();
   658→
   659→    // if (error) {
   660→    //     if (showSerial)
   661→    //         Serial.print(DevUtils::termColor("red") + "Failed trying to deserialize placeholder_rates.json with error: " + error.c_str() + DevUtils::termColor("reset") + "\n");
   662→    //     return "1.000e+03";
   663→    // }
   664→
   665→    // print all keys in jsonBuffer
   666→    // Serial.println("Printing all keys in jsonBuffer...");
   667→    // for (const auto& pair : spacecraftPlaceholderRatesJson.as<JsonObject>()) {
   668→    //     Serial.println(pair.key().c_str());
   669→    // }
   670→
   671→
   672→    
   673→    if (spacecraftPlaceholderRatesJson.containsKey(key)) {
   674→        if (showSerial)
   675→            Serial.println(DevUtils::termColor("green") +  "Found spacecraft rate for " + String(key) + DevUtils::termColor("reset") + "\n\n");
   676→        
   677→        // Get JsonVariant at key
   678→        JsonVariant variant = spacecraftPlaceholderRatesJson[key];
   679→
   680→        // Check if the JsonVariant is an array
   681→        if (variant.is<JsonArray>()) {
   682→            JsonArray arr = variant.as<JsonArray>();
   683→
   684→            // Generate a random index within the bounds of the array using random8
   685→            int randomIndex = random8(arr.size());
   686→
   687→            if (showSerial) {
   688→                Serial.println("Choosing placeholder rate...");
   689→                // Serial.println("Random index: " + String(randomIndex));
   690→                // Serial.println("Array size: " + String(arr.size()));
   691→
   692→                // print all items in array
   693→                uint8_t placeholderCounter = 0;
   694→                for (JsonVariant v : arr) {
   695→                    if (placeholderCounter == randomIndex) {
   696→                        Serial.print("> ");
   697→                    } else {
   698→                        Serial.print("  ");
   699→                    }
   700→                    Serial.println(v.as<String>());
   701→                    placeholderCounter++;
   702→                }
   703→                Serial.print("\n\n");
   704→            }
   705→
   706→            // Get the rate at the random index
   707→            const char* spacecraftRate = arr[randomIndex];
   708→
   709→            if (showSerial)
   710→                Serial.println("Spacecraft rate: " + String(spacecraftRate));
   711→
   712→            return spacecraftRate;
   713→        } else {
   714→            if (showSerial)
   715→                Serial.println("It's not an array");
   716→            // If it's not an array, assume it's a single rate and return it
   717→            const char* spacecraftRate = variant.as<const char*>();
   718→            return spacecraftRate;
   719→        }
   720→    }
   721→
   722→    if (showSerial)
   723→        Serial.println(DevUtils::termColor("red") + "Spacecraft rate not found for " + String(key) + DevUtils::termColor("reset") + "\n\n");
   724→
   725→    // Spacecraft rate not found, return the default rate
   726→    return "1.000e+03";
   727→}

     6→/* Initialize global brightness */
     7→int AnimationUtils::brightness = 16;
     8→
     9→AnimationUtils::AnimationUtils()
    10→{
    11→	// be happy
    12→}
    13→
    14→/* Constructor - set brightness potentiometer pin */
    15→AnimationUtils::AnimationUtils(int pin)
    16→{
    17→	potPin = pin;
    18→}
    19→
    20→/* Read brightness potentiometer
    21→ * Read potentiometer for global brightness value
    22→ *
    23→ * @return Potentiometer value mapped to 0-255
    24→ */
    25→int AnimationUtils::readBrightness()
    26→{
    27→	int potValue = analogRead(potPin); // Read potentiometer value
    28→	potValue = constrain(potValue, 0, 127);	// Constrain potentiometer value to 0-127 so brightness won't wrap around
    29→	int potBrightness = map(potValue, 0, 127, 8, 255); // Map potentiometer value to 8-255 for brightness - less than 8 causes flickering
    30→	int hardcodedBrightness = 32; // Hardcoded brightness value for testing
    31→	return potBrightness;
    32→}
    33→
    34→/* Set global brightness value based on poteniometer value */
    35→void AnimationUtils::updateBrightness(int brightness)
    36→{
    37→	brightness = constrain(brightness, 8, 255); // Constrain brightness to 8-255
    38→	FileUtils::config.displayLED.brightness = brightness; // Update global brightness value
    39→	FastLED.setBrightness(brightness);
    40→}
    41→

    59→void FileUtils::listDir(const char* dirname, uint8_t levels) {
    60→	Serial.printf("Listing directory: %s\r\n", dirname);
    61→
    62→	File root = LittleFS.open(dirname);
    63→	if (!root) {
    64→		Serial.println("- failed to open directory");
    65→		return;
    66→	}
    67→	if (!root.isDirectory()) {
    68→		Serial.println(" - not a directory");
    69→		return;
    70→	}
    71→
    72→	File file = root.openNextFile();
    73→	while (file) {
    74→		if (file.isDirectory()) {
    75→			Serial.print("  DIR : ");
    76→
    77→			Serial.print(file.name());
    78→			time_t t = file.getLastWrite();
    79→			struct tm* tmstruct = localtime(&t);
    80→			Serial.printf("  LAST WRITE: %d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d:%02d\n", (tmstruct->tm_year) + 1900, (tmstruct->tm_mon) + 1, tmstruct->tm_mday, tmstruct->tm_hour, tmstruct->tm_min, tmstruct->tm_sec);
    81→
    82→			if (levels) {
    83→				listDir(file.name(), levels - 1);
    84→			}
    85→		} else {
    86→			Serial.print("  FILE: ");
    87→			Serial.print(file.name());
    88→			Serial.print("  SIZE: ");
    89→
    90→			Serial.print(file.size());
    91→			time_t t = file.getLastWrite();
    92→			struct tm* tmstruct = localtime(&t);
    93→			Serial.printf("  LAST WRITE: %d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d:%02d\n", (tmstruct->tm_year) + 1900, (tmstruct->tm_mon) + 1, tmstruct->tm_mday, tmstruct->tm_hour, tmstruct->tm_min, tmstruct->tm_sec);
    94→		}
    95→		file = root.openNextFile();
    96→	}
    97→}

---

Reviewing the JPL-MiniPulse ESP32 firmware project. This covers `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp` and all libraries under `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/lib/`.

---

## Critical Issues

### 1. Queue created AFTER the task that uses it (Null pointer dereference / crash)

**File:** `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp`, lines 3495-3504

**Confidence: 100**

The `getData` task is pinned to core 0 at line 3495 before the queue is created at line 3504. The task's `getData()` function references `queue` on line 3169 (`uxQueueSpacesAvailable(queue)`). If the task wakes up before `queue = xQueueCreate(...)` executes on core 1, it will call FreeRTOS queue functions on a NULL handle, causing a crash or undefined behavior.

```cpp
// Line 3495 - task created BEFORE queue exists
xTaskCreatePinnedToCore(getData, "getData", 6144, NULL, 0, &xHandleData, 0);

// Line 3504 - queue created AFTER
queue = xQueueCreate(5, sizeof(CraftQueueItem));
```

**Fix:** Create the queue before creating the task, or gate `getData` on `queue != NULL` as the very first check inside the task loop.

---

### 2. Semaphore assignment bug: `==` instead of `=` (mutex never released)

**File:** `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp`, lines 2746 and 2767

**Confidence: 100**

Two separate code paths use the comparison operator `==` where assignment `=` is required. This means `semaphoreTaken` is never set to `false`, and on the next call to `parseData()` the function will attempt to re-acquire a mutex that is already held (or behave incorrectly in edge cases).

```cpp
// Line 2746 - comparison, not assignment
semaphoreTaken == false;   // BUG: should be semaphoreTaken = false;

// Line 2767 - same bug in unreachable dead code path
semaphoreTaken == false;   // BUG
```

Both are dead code paths in normal execution, but the one at line 2746 is the "success" path after `incrementDataParseCounter()` — the mutex is given back but `semaphoreTaken` stays `true`, which means the catch-block at line 2733 will call `xSemaphoreGive` again on an already-given mutex on the next parse error.

---

### 3. Queue sends a pointer to a stack-allocated item (dangling pointer / data corruption)

**File:** `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp`, lines 2200, 3558

**Confidence: 100**

`xQueueCreate` is called with `sizeof(CraftQueueItem)` at line 3504, meaning the queue is designed to store full structs by value. However at line 2200, `xQueueSend` is called with `&newCraft` where `newCraft` is a `CraftQueueItem*`. This sends the pointer to the pointer, not the struct data:

```cpp
// Line 2200 - sends a CraftQueueItem** (pointer-to-pointer), not the struct
if (xQueueSend(queue, &newCraft, 100) == pdPASS) {
```

At line 3558, the receive side uses `&infoBuffer` where `infoBuffer` is also a pointer, compounding the mismatch. The queue reads 4 bytes (pointer size) into a 144-byte struct slot, leaving the rest of the received struct with garbage data.

**Fix:** Send and receive the struct directly:
```cpp
xQueueSend(queue, newCraft, 100);   // send struct by value
xQueueReceive(queue, infoBuffer, 1); // receive into struct
```

---

### 4. `assignValuesToCraftSemaphore` iterates backwards but always reads from `freeListTop` (wrong item allocated)

**File:** `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp`, lines 2257-2286

**Confidence: 95**

The loop iterates `i` from `MAX_ITEMS - 1` down to `1`, checks `freeList[i] != nullptr`, but then always reads from `freeList[freeListTop]` instead of `freeList[i]`. If `freeListTop` and `i` don't coincide, it may pick a null or wrong pool item, and it always overwrites the same item regardless of which slot was found to be free.

```cpp
for (uint8_t i = MAX_ITEMS - 1; i > 0; i--) {
    if (freeList[i] != nullptr) {
        newCraft = freeList[freeListTop]; // BUG: should be freeList[i]
        ...
    }
}
```

Additionally, `newCraft` is declared but never initialized, so if the loop finds no free items it is returned uninitialized.

---

### 5. OTA firmware update uses plain HTTP over an unencrypted connection

**File:** `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp`, lines 451, 503

**Confidence: 95**

Both the version check and firmware download use `http://develop.kellerdigital.com/...`. An attacker on the same network (or via DNS spoofing) can serve a malicious firmware binary and fully compromise the device. The DSN data URL in `FileUtils.cpp` line 16 correctly uses HTTPS, making the OTA inconsistency more notable.

```cpp
httpFirmware.begin("http://develop.kellerdigital.com/minipulse/latest_version.txt");
httpUpdate.update(client, "http://develop.kellerdigital.com/minipulse/firmware.bin");
```

**Fix:** Use `https://` and a `WiFiClientSecure` with certificate validation for both calls.

---

### 6. Static 20 KB stack-allocated buffer in a FreeRTOS task (stack overflow risk)

**File:** `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp`, line 3031

**Confidence: 95**

## Critical Issues

### 1. Queue created AFTER the task that uses it (Null pointer dereference / crash)

**File:** `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp`, lines 3495-3504

**Confidence: 100**

The `getData` task is pinned to core 0 at line 3495 before the queue is created at line 3504. The task's `getData()` function references `queue` on line 3169 (`uxQueueSpacesAvailable(queue)`). If the task wakes up before `queue = xQueueCreate(...)` executes on core 1, it will call FreeRTOS queue functions on a NULL handle, causing a crash or undefined behavior.

```cpp
// Line 3495 - task created BEFORE queue exists
xTaskCreatePinnedToCore(getData, "getData", 6144, NULL, 0, &xHandleData, 0);

// Line 3504 - queue created AFTER
queue = xQueueCreate(5, sizeof(CraftQueueItem));
```

**Fix:** Create the queue before creating the task, or gate `getData` on `queue != NULL` as the very first check inside the task loop.

### 2. Semaphore assignment bug: `==` instead of `=` (mutex never released)

**File:** `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp`, lines 2746 and 2767

**Confidence: 100**

Two separate code paths use the comparison operator `==` where assignment `=` is required. This means `semaphoreTaken` is never set to `false`, and on the next call to `parseData()` the function will attempt to re-acquire a mutex that is already held (or behave incorrectly in edge cases).

```cpp
// Line 2746 - comparison, not assignment
semaphoreTaken == false;   // BUG: should be semaphoreTaken = false;

// Line 2767 - same bug in unreachable dead code path
semaphoreTaken == false;   // BUG
```

Both are dead code paths in normal execution, but the one at line 2746 is the "success" path after `incrementDataParseCounter()` — the mutex is given back but `semaphoreTaken` stays `true`, which means the catch-block at line 2733 will call `xSemaphoreGive` again on an already-given mutex on the next parse error.

### 3. Queue sends a pointer to a stack-allocated item (dangling pointer / data corruption)

**File:** `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp`, lines 2200, 3558

**Confidence: 100**

`xQueueCreate` is called with `sizeof(CraftQueueItem)` at line 3504, meaning the queue is designed to store full structs by value. However at line 2200, `xQueueSend` is called with `&newCraft` where `newCraft` is a `CraftQueueItem*`. This sends the pointer to the pointer, not the struct data:

```cpp
// Line 2200 - sends a CraftQueueItem** (pointer-to-pointer), not the struct
if (xQueueSend(queue, &newCraft, 100) == pdPASS) {
```

At line 3558, the receive side uses `&infoBuffer` where `infoBuffer` is also a pointer, compounding the mismatch. The queue reads 4 bytes (pointer size) into a 144-byte struct slot, leaving the rest of the received struct with garbage data.

**Fix:** Send and receive the struct directly:
```cpp
xQueueSend(queue, newCraft, 100);   // send struct by value
xQueueReceive(queue, infoBuffer, 1); // receive into struct
```

```

If it succeeds, `LittleFS.begin(true)` is called again at line 3219, with a hardcoded `true` which means it will **format the filesystem every reboot** if called a second time with `true`. The `FORMAT_LITTLEFS_IF_FAILED` flag at line 71 is `#define FORMAT_LITTLEFS_IF_FAILED true`, so both calls pass `true`, and the second call's side effects depend on the LittleFS implementation.

In practice this is likely a copy-paste artifact and the second call should just check a return value or be removed, as the filesystem is already mounted.

# JPL-MiniPulse -- Comprehensive Architectural Analysis

## Executive Summary

JPL-MiniPulse is a well-conceived embedded system that fetches live NASA Deep Space Network telemetry and renders spacecraft communication data as LED animations across 2,565 WS2812B pixels on four concentric rings. The architecture leverages ESP32 dual-core FreeRTOS effectively, with a clean producer/consumer split between data acquisition (Core 0) and rendering (Core 1).

**Quality Score: 6.5/10** -- The system works and demonstrates strong domain understanding, but suffers from a monolithic main.cpp (~3,650 lines), significant commented-out code debris, configuration duplication between compile-time constants and the runtime config system, and several concurrency safety issues in the semaphore/queue memory pool.

---

## 1. Overall Architecture and Design Patterns

### Architecture Pattern: Producer-Consumer with Dual-Core Split

The system follows a classic **producer-consumer** pattern mediated by a FreeRTOS queue:

```
Core 0 (Producer)             FreeRTOS Queue            Core 1 (Consumer)
getData() task       --->   xQueueCreate(5)    --->    loop() dequeues
  fetchData()                                           updateAnimation()
  parseData()                                           scrollLetters()
  xQueueSend()                                          doRateBasedAnimation()
                                                        drawMeteors()
                                                        FastLED.show()
```

**Strengths:**
- Clean separation of I/O-bound work (HTTP fetch, XML parse) from real-time rendering
- The queue provides natural back-pressure (max 5 items)
- Watchdog timer integration prevents hangs on either core

**Weaknesses:**
- The "architecture" lives almost entirely in a single 3,652-line file (`/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp`). Functions for WiFi management, OTA updates, animation logic, data parsing, serial debugging, and LED rendering are all interleaved in one monolith.
- No formal state machine governs the lifecycle transitions (boot -> WiFi connect -> data fetch -> animate -> transition). States are tracked via scattered boolean flags (`nameScrollDone`, `animationInProgress`, `animationTypeSetDown`, `animateFirstCycleDown`, `dataStarted`, `portalRunning`, `otaUpdateTriggered`, `usingDummyData`, `forceDummyData`).

### Design Patterns Identified

| Pattern | Location | Assessment |
|---------|----------|------------|
| Producer-Consumer | `getData()` / `loop()` | Good, well-suited to dual-core |
| Object Pool (Free List) | `itemPool[]`, `freeList[]`, `freeListMutex` (main.cpp:261-264) | Partially implemented, has safety issues |
| Strategy (Animation) | `rateClassSettings[]` lookup tables (main.cpp:1541-1650) | Data-driven, clean |
| Singleton (Config) | `FileUtils::config` static struct (FileUtils.h:104) | Appropriate for embedded |
| Template Method | `doRateBasedAnimation()` dispatches to sub-patterns (main.cpp:1653) | Clean branching |

---

| **Animate** | `lib/Animate/Animate.{h,cpp}` | 220 | Meteor rendering engine | Depends on AnimationUtils, MathHelpers, FastLED |
| **AnimationUtils** | `lib/AnimationUtils/AnimationUtils.{h,cpp}` | 130 | Color definitions, brightness control | Depends on FileUtils, FastLED, MathHelpers |

### Separation of Concerns Assessment

**Well-separated:**
- `MathHelpers` -- pure utility, zero coupling
- `TextCharacters` -- pure data module, no side effects
- `FileUtils` -- clean abstraction over LittleFS with config management

**Poorly separated:**
- **`src/main.cpp` is the critical problem.** At ~3,650 lines, it contains animation orchestration, data fetching, HTTP handling, XML parsing, WiFi management, OTA updates, queue management, semaphore pool management, serial debugging utilities, and the main loop. At minimum, these should be extracted:
  - `DataFetcher` module (fetchData, fetchHTTPData, generateFetchUrl, handleHttpResponse)
  - `DataParser` module (parseData, findSignals, rateLongToRateClass)
  - `AnimationController` module (doRateBasedAnimation, createMeteor, all animation pattern functions)
  - `WiFiController` module (doWiFiManager, webServerCallback, saveParamsCallback)
  - `OTAUpdater` module (setupOtaUpdate, updateFirmwareOta, checkFirmwareUpdateAvailable)

- **SpacecraftData has a redundant write-then-read cycle.** The `loadSpacecraftNamesFile()` method at `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/lib/SpacecraftData/SpacecraftData.cpp:155-192` first calls `createAndWriteNamesFile()` which populates the in-memory JSON document AND writes it to a file, then immediately reads it back from the file and deserializes it again. The data is already in memory after `createAndWriteNamesFile()` completes. The same pattern repeats for blacklist and placeholder rates.

- **Commented-out code volume.** `SpacecraftData.h` lines 67-124 contain an entire duplicate class definition. `SpacecraftData.cpp` lines 734-907 contain hundreds of lines of commented-out PROGMEM implementations. `main.cpp` has extensive commented-out WiFi parameter code (lines 278-344).

## 4. FreeRTOS Task Architecture

### Task Layout

| Task | Core | Stack | Priority | Function |
|------|------|-------|----------|----------|
| `getData` | Core 0 | 6,144 bytes | 0 (idle) | Data acquisition and parsing |
| Arduino `loop()` | Core 1 | Default (8,192) | 1 | WiFi, animation, LED output |

**Created at** `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp:3495-3502`:
```cpp
xTaskCreatePinnedToCore(getData, "getData", 6144, NULL, 0, &xHandleData, 0);
```

### Queue Configuration

**Created at** `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp:3504`:
```cpp
queue = xQueueCreate(5, sizeof(CraftQueueItem));
```

The queue holds `CraftQueueItem` structs (144 bytes each: 40-byte callsign + 100-byte name + 4 bytes metadata). 5 items = ~720 bytes of queue storage.

### Semaphore / Mutex Usage

**`freeListMutex`** (created at main.cpp:3485): Protects the `freeList[]` object pool for `CraftQueueItem` allocation.

### Critical Concurrency Issues

1. **Race condition in `assignValuesToCraftSemaphore()`.** At `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp:2248-2287`, this function accesses `freeList[]` and `freeListTop` but does NOT acquire `freeListMutex`. It is called from within `parseData()` which DOES hold the mutex (line 2387), but the function signature gives no indication it must be called under lock. This is fragile.

2. **Comparison instead of assignment bug.** At `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp:2746`:
   ```cpp
   semaphoreTaken == false;  // BUG: should be semaphoreTaken = false;
   ```
   This is a comparison expression used as a statement -- the value is never assigned. The same bug appears at line 2767. This means `semaphoreTaken` may remain `true` after the mutex is released, potentially causing the mutex to be given back a second time in the catch block at line 2733-2736.

3. **`freeListTop` boundary conditions.** At `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp:2254-2255`:
   ```cpp
   if (freeListTop < 0) freeListTop = 0;
   if (freeListTop >= MAX_ITEMS) freeListTop = MAX_ITEMS - 1;
   ```
   These clamp operations silently mask bugs rather than failing visibly. If `freeListTop` goes negative, it means a double-free or underflow occurred.

4. **Task priority inversion risk.** The `getData` task runs at priority 0 (idle priority). If Core 0 has any other work (WiFi stack background tasks run on Core 0), the data fetch task could be starved. In practice the ESP32 Arduino WiFi stack does run tasks on Core 0.

5. **`printCurrentQueue()` is destructive.** At `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp:651-710`, the debug function dequeues all items from the main queue into a temporary queue and back. If called from Core 1 while Core 0 is also accessing the queue, this creates a race condition. The temporary queue creation (`xQueueCreate(5, sizeof(CraftQueueItem))`) also allocates heap memory in a debug function, which is risky in low-memory situations.

6. **Watchdog timeout is very long.** At `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/src/main.cpp:3519`:
   ```cpp
   esp_task_wdt_init(60, true);
   ```
   A 60-second watchdog means the system could be unresponsive for a full minute before recovery. The data parsing loops include `vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(100))` calls to yield, but these are inside deeply nested loops with `feedWatchdog()` calls scattered throughout, suggesting past issues with watchdog timeouts.

### Dynamic Allocations

| Allocation | When | Location | Freed |
|------------|------|----------|-------|
| `new Meteor{...}` | Every animation burst | main.cpp:1241 | `delete thisMeteor` at main.cpp:1902 |
| `DynamicJsonDocument` internals | Boot-time | SpacecraftData.cpp:3-5 | Never (static lifetime) |
| `String` concatenations | Throughout | Multiple | Arduino String manages |
| `malloc()` in `logOutput()` | Each debug log call | main.cpp:2794 | `free()` at main.cpp:2805 |
| `xQueueCreate()` in `printCurrentQueue()` | Debug function | main.cpp:664 | `vQueueDelete()` at main.cpp:703 |

### Memory Concerns

1. **Meteor heap allocation churn.** Each animation cycle creates multiple `Meteor` objects on the heap via `new` (main.cpp:1241) and deletes them when they finish animating (main.cpp:1902). With `ActiveMeteorArraySize = 500` slots and animations repeating every ~3 seconds, this creates significant heap fragmentation over time. A fixed pool allocator for Meteor objects would be safer.

2. **Arduino String usage in an embedded context.** Functions like `logOutput()` (main.cpp:2781), `printFreeHeap()` (DevUtils.cpp:64), and many serial print calls use Arduino `String` concatenation, which allocates and deallocates heap memory. In the `DevUtils::termColor()` function at `/Users/grant/code/JPL-MiniPulse/lib/DevUtils/DevUtils.cpp:4`, the return type is `String` (heap-allocated), but the actual data is `const char*` (static). This causes unnecessary allocations every time a color code is requested.

3. **`xmlDataBuffer[20480]` as static local.** Declared inside `fetchData()` at main.cpp:3031 with `static` keyword, this 20KB buffer lives for the entire program lifetime. This is appropriate for embedded (avoids stack overflow), but it means 20KB of RAM is permanently reserved even when not actively parsing.

4. **ESP32 has ~320KB total SRAM.** With LED buffers consuming ~7.7KB, JSON documents ~12.3KB, XML buffer ~20KB, and other allocations, the firmware uses roughly 40-50KB of statically allocated RAM before accounting for stack space, FreeRTOS internals, WiFi buffers, and heap. The `ESP.getFreeHeap()` monitoring (visible in diagnostics mode) is appropriate for tracking this.
